output.headline: Ratifies up to $20,400 for medical staff at Oakland Athletic League high school sports events
output.summary: The district pays a contractor to schedule and provide approved medical personnel, such as athletic trainers, at high school sports events run by the Oakland Athletic League. The cost is capped at $20,400 for April 1 through June 30, 2021. The Board is approving this after the contract period began.

output.headline: Adds $5,200 for Bay Area Community Resources summer program at Esperanza Elementary School
output.summary: This adds $5,200.00 to a 2020-2021 memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Bay Area Community Resources for 20 days of summer 2021 programming at Esperanza Elementary School, weekdays from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m. It raises the not-to-exceed amount from $103,853.00 to $109,053.00. The agreement period is August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Adds $15,600 for Ujimaa Foundation summer program at Burckhalter Elementary School
output.summary: This adds $15,600.00 to a 2020-2021 memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Ujimaa Foundation for 24 days of summer 2021 programming at Burckhalter Elementary School, weekdays from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m. It raises the not-to-exceed amount from $39,204.00 to $54,804.00. The agreement period is August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Adds $20,800 for Bay Area Community Resources summer program at Madison Park Academy Upper Campus
output.summary: This adds $20,800.00 to a 2020-2021 memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Bay Area Community Resources for 20 days of summer 2021 programming at Madison Park Academy Upper Campus, weekdays from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m. It raises the not-to-exceed amount from $222,134.00 to $242,934.00. The agreement period is August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $15,600 for Acta Non Verba to run summer learning at EnCompass Academy
output.summary: The district pays Acta Non Verba to provide summer learning program services and supports for students at the EnCompass Academy hub, up to $15,600. The work runs June 1 through July 15, 2021. The Board is ratifying this agreement after the start date.

output.headline: Adds $44,460 for Bay Area Community Resources summer program at Elmhurst United Middle School
output.summary: This adds $44,460.00 to a 2020-2021 memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Bay Area Community Resources for 19 days of summer 2021 programming at Elmhurst United Middle School, weekdays from 12 p.m. to 3 p.m. It raises the not-to-exceed amount from $185,442.00 to $229,902.00. The agreement period is August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021, and all other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Approves up to $80,190 for Jensen Hughes fire and intrusion alarm design at East Oakland Pride Elementary
output.summary: The district hires Jensen Hughes to design the fire and intrusion alarm project at East Oakland Pride Elementary School and administer construction, including help with bidding. The cost is capped at $80,190, which includes a $7,290 contingency fee. Work is scheduled from June 3, 2021 to May 31, 2022.

output.headline: Approves $80,190 for Jensen Hughes fire and intrusion alarm design at Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary
schools: Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School
output.summary: The district hires Jensen Hughes to design the fire and intrusion alarm project at Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School and administer construction, including help with bidding. The amount is $80,190, which includes a $7,290 contingency fee. Work is scheduled from June 3, 2021 to May 31, 2022.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $15,600 for Nexplore to run summer learning at Rise Community School
output.summary: The district pays Nexplore, a Florida company, to provide summer learning program services and supports for students at the Rise Community School hub, up to $15,600. The work runs June 7 through July 9, 2021. The Board is ratifying this agreement.

output.headline: Approves up to $26,000 for Lincoln to run summer learning at West Oakland Middle School
output.summary: The district pays Lincoln to provide summer learning program services and supports for students at the West Oakland Middle School hub, up to $26,000. The work runs June 7 through July 2, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies $17,054 more for InPlay's student data reports and tools, raising the cap to $47,054
output.summary: This amendment adds $17,054 to a 2020-2021 agreement with UnaMesa Association (doing business as InPlay), raising the not-to-exceed amount from $30,000 to $47,054. The added work is more reports and views, separate tools for Bridge programs, editable student data in the Summer Learning registration tool, and a process to notify staff of changes to student data. The period is December 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $10,777.22 for DocuSign e-signature software for expanded learning and partnership offices
output.summary: The district pays DocuSign for its eSignature software and premier support for the Expanded Learning and Community Partnerships offices, up to $10,777.22. The subscription runs May 15, 2021 through May 14, 2022. The Board is ratifying this after the start date.

output.headline: Alameda County Office of Education supports career pathways at Castlemont High at no cost
output.summary: The Alameda County Office of Education will provide state-funded K12 Strong Workforce Program support for the Sustainable Urban Design Academy and Community Health Equity Academy career pathways at Castlemont High School. There is no cost to the district. The agreement period is July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $2,000 for equity coaching sessions for Greenleaf Elementary school leaders
output.summary: The district pays a Denver consultant for up to eight coaching sessions that support Greenleaf Elementary school leaders in carrying out diversity, equity and inclusion strategies after earlier training sessions. The cost is capped at $2,000 for January 4 through May 31, 2021. The Board is ratifying this after the work began.

output.headline: Partners with CalStateTEACH to place teaching interns in district classrooms through 2024
output.summary: The district signs a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with CalStateTEACH, a California State University teaching credential program, for intern partnership and practica programs in K-12 multiple-subject teaching. The agreement runs July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024. The text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Adds $55,300 for Bay Area Community Resources to supervise student mentors at Oakland Tech
output.summary: This amendment adds $55,300 to a 2020-2021 agreement with Bay Area Community Resources, raising the not-to-exceed amount from $333,270 to $388,570. The added money covers supervision of five Student Support Specialists who give extra academic mentoring to pathway students affected by the COVID pandemic. The period is August 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $9,750 for three health-pathway murals at Life Academy
output.summary: The district pays an Oakland artist to design and paint three murals at Life Academy, one for each health and bioscience pathway: biotech, health and medicine, and public health. The cost is capped at $9,750 for May 3 through June 30, 2021. The Board is ratifying this after the work began.

output.headline: Ratifies $2,600 more for Inner City Bliss meditation classes at Dewey Academy
output.summary: This amendment adds $2,600 for an additional eight-week program of beginner to advanced meditation instruction for Dewey Academy students, tied to health and medical career technical education standards. It raises the agreement from $3,200 to a not-to-exceed amount of $5,800. The period is February 1 through May 28, 2021.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $9,300 for media materials to attract students to engineering and computer science pathways
output.summary: The district pays an Oakland contractor to develop print and video materials, in line with the goals of the 2020-2021 Intel grant, to attract a diverse group of students to the Engineering and Computer Science Linked Learning pathways. The cost is capped at $9,300 for May 3 through June 30, 2021. The Board is ratifying this after the start date.

output.headline: Ratifies up to $10,000 for Boxing for Health virtual boxing classes at LaEscuelita Elementary
output.summary: The district pays Boxing for Health for virtual boxing classes at LaEscuelita Elementary School, 2 hours per week (4 class sessions per week) for 9 weeks, up to $10,000. The period is March 17 through May 31, 2021. The Board is ratifying this after the start date.

output.headline: Accepts $150,000 from the Walter & Elise Haas Fund to expand summer internships for career pathways
output.summary: The district accepts a $150,000 grant from the Walter & Elise Haas Fund to expand staffing for the Exploring College, Career, and Community Options summer internship program. The grant also supports connections with private industry for Oakland youth in career pathways. The grant period is April 14, 2021 through April 13, 2022.

output.headline: Extends First 5 Alameda County kindergarten readiness grant to June 2022 at the same $896,670
output.summary: This amendment to a First 5 Alameda County grant contract swaps in revised program descriptions and payment terms and extends the contract from June 30, 2021 to June 30, 2022. The amount stays at $896,670, so no new money is added. The grant supports kindergarten readiness through the Neighborhood Ready for School program.

output.headline: Approves up to $758,625 for Goalbook through 2024 without public bidding
output.summary: The Board approves a resolution allowing the district to skip public bidding (a sole source exception) and signs a services agreement with Enome, Inc., doing business as Goalbook, for up to $758,625. The agreement runs February 1, 2021 through June 30, 2024. The action text does not describe the service; the item was filed by the Special Education Department.

output.headline: Ratifies a student data privacy agreement with Educational Results Partnership for Cal-PASS Plus
output.summary: The district ratifies a data privacy agreement with Educational Results Partnership of Sacramento. It spells out the group's duties to protect student data sent to it through Cal-PASS Plus, including following federal and California student privacy laws. It stays in effect as long as the district takes part in Cal-PASS Plus or the group holds any student data. No dollar amount is stated.
